articles.title_zh: Voters in Brazil head to polls as Lula goes up against Bolsonaro's son
facts_zh:
Voters in Brazil head to polls as Lula goes up against Bolsonaro's son
- Published
Polls have opened in Brazil as people choose their new president in a closely fought run-off election.
The choice is between the 80-year-old incumbent, left-winger Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term in office, and right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro, 45.
Bolsonaro is the son of former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, who was sentenced to more than 20 years in jail for plotting a coup after losing the last election in 2022.

articles.title_original: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
articles.title_zh: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
facts_zh:
El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
- Published
Four bodies handed over to special forces on a mission to Haiti to recover Salvadoran hostages are "not our men", El Salvador's president has said.

Nayib Bukele said a nongovernmental organisation delivered the human remains to one of Haiti's airports claiming they were four El Salvadoran air technicians, but that one of the corpses was a child's and another was wearing a different country's army uniform.
He had dispatched a military contingent, reportedly of hundreds of soldiers, on Thursday after the four men vanished after being ambushed by "heavily armed criminal groups".

- Published
Elon Musk has said his company SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink internet service, after Ukrainian officials said connectivity issues appeared to have been resolved.

The tech billionaire accused Ukraine of violating its terms of service by using it for military activity - but denied being responsible for a simultaneous issue with its US-run, military-grade counterpart Starshield.
Kyiv has not officially commented on Musk's latest claim but Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said his post was "very strange".

facts_zh:
Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates
- Published
All West Bank land crossings will be closed during Tuesday's election in Israel, the country's military says, and Palestinian workers will be barred from entering all settlements.
The restrictions come amid a crackdown in the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the territory.

The Israel Defense Forces announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday.

articles.title_zh: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in north-east Nigeria
facts_zh:
Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in north-east Nigeria
- Published
Unknown gunmen have raided a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba, killing at least 10 people, looting shops and setting houses ablaze, police say.
There are fears the actual death toll is much higher, with eyewitnesses speaking of 20 lives lost and a non-governmental organisation suggesting a toll of as many as 50.
The gunmen reportedly swooped on the village of Binnari in the Karim Lamido area mounted on motorcycles just after midday Muslim prayers on Friday in a rampage that went on for up to four hours.

articles.title_zh: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
facts_zh:
Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
- Published
Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said.

After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux.
But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history.

articles.title_original: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
articles.title_zh: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
facts_zh:
Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
- Published
Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.

Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free".
Following the Instagram post on Friday, Vanessa and Kai Trump released a longer video on Saturday, in which they discussed breast cancer awareness, early detection and prevention.

all_titles.en: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis

articles.title_original: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
articles.title_zh: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
facts_zh:
Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
- Published
Two people have been pulled alive from the rubble of a building that collapsed in Kenya's capital, Nairobi, on Friday, as a search continues for five still missing.
Police said on Saturday that a manhunt had been launched for the building's owner and the contractor responsible for the site.
Dramatic footage shows the bottom floor of the block, thought to have been 16 or 18 storeys, giving way before the rest of the building crumples, sending a plume of dust into the surrounding streets.

all_titles.en: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing

articles.title_zh: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas
facts_zh:
Mum who died trying to save sons was hero, husband says
- Published
The husband of a British woman who died rescuing their sons when they were swept away to sea in the Bahamas says she was a "hero...
in life and in death".
Leanne Gregory, from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire, had been snorkelling with her family when the boys were swept away by a strong current, police said.

articles.title_original: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
articles.title_zh: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
facts_zh:
Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
- Published
Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest.
Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames.
Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene where the blaze was still burning early on Saturday, as police said difficult terrain hindered efforts to bring the fire under control.

all_titles.en: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
